public_rationale: Earlier chess and program studies provide substantial evidence that useful internal world representations can emerge. Other experiments find serious coherence failures. Neither side establishes the broader claim about proper, stable models in the specified observation period. Reading the sentence as denying any learned world representation would make it much easier to contradict, but that would discard qualifications supplied by the essay.
limitations: All cited experiments precede the selected observation window and are context only.
Specialized sequence models may not represent the intended population of general-purpose LLMs.
The verdict depends on what completeness and stability proper requires.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Proper world models do not emerge on their own in LLMs.

statement.excerpt: One hopes that proper world models will simply “emerge” — but they don’t.
statement.document_title: Generative AI’s crippling and widespread failure to induce robust models of the world

our_interpretation: This is a claim about the state of LLMs at publication, not a prediction that emergence is forever impossible.
In context, proper means a coherent internal representation that tracks a domain and can be updated and used. A probe decoding some information is insufficient by itself.
An identifiable distributed representation can qualify; I do not require a hand-written symbolic database or perfect performance.

Because no observation period is named, I use June 2025 through publication as the latest monthly observation window. Earlier experiments are background evidence rather than direct measurements in that window.
criteria.support_condition: Representative tests of relevant models show that apparent representations fail coherent state tracking, updating, and causal-use tests across the domains covered by the claim.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A relevant model develops, through ordinary predictive training without an explicitly supplied world-model mechanism, a coherent and updatable internal representation that demonstrably guides behavior in a nontrivial domain.

evidence.explanation: The model learns board representations through character prediction, and interventions change its moves. This materially weakens an unrestricted denial of emergence, but predates the observation window and does not establish every aspect of a complete, stable chess model.

evidence.publisher: Charles Jin and Martin Rinard, ICML 2024; arXiv
evidence.explanation: The experiments recover intermediate grid-world states and address whether the probe itself learns the semantics. This is positive evidence in a restricted synthetic environment, rather than a June 2025 assessment of general-purpose LLMs.

Earlier navigation experiments show that successful predictions can coexist with incoherent inferred maps. They support skepticism about some apparent world models, but cannot establish universal nonemergence.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representation, updating, and causal-intervention tests on identifiable models from the target period, with a stated domain and robustness standard sufficient to distinguish a maintained world model from partial correlates.
